title: Initial examination of the Need for Chaos (Revised) Scale in German.
abstract: The termrefers to an individual's mindset demonstrating a desire for the destruction of the established order and the societal structures. This novel construct may be of relevance for forensic, legal, and safety matters as well as politics. To measure differences in individuals' need for chaos, the seven-items NFCScale was developed in English. Later two items were added to create the recently proposed nine-items NFCScale. In the present study ( = 817), we present German adaptations of those two scales and an initial examination of their psychometric properties. For the German seven-items NFCScale, we found a two-dimensional structure with the factorsandwhich were strongly and positively interrelated. The semantic content of the two additional items of the German nine-items NFCScale and the statistical analyses suggest that these items capture yet another construct (i.e.,). Furthermore, results preliminary indicate sufficient reliability and validity of both German adaptations. Dark personality measures (e.g., dark core, psychopathy), left-wing authoritarian antihierarchical aggression, radicalism intention (i.e., the intention to use illegal and violent means for political ends), and the inclination to justify political violence emerged as substantial correlates of the need for chaos in our German-speaking sample.
